images.title: An arrow turning from down to left
images.purpose: Show an arrow that points down and makes a quarter turn to point left, and a small clock showing that the turn goes the way a clock moves from 6 to 9, which is clockwise.
images.composition: Two arrows with a curved arrow between them on the left, a small clock on the right, and the answer written below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. LEFT DIAGRAM, centre point (420, 360) shown as a dark dot 26 px across. A teal #0072B2 arrow (12 px line with a solid arrowhead, 220 px long) goes straight down from the centre, labelled start (34 px, bold, dark) at (440, 620). An amber #E69F00 arrow (12 px line with a solid arrowhead, 220 px long) goes straight left from the centre, labelled after a quarter turn (34 px, bold, dark) at (130, 330). A curved amber arrow with an arrowhead on a circle of radius 120 px runs from the down arrow round to the left arrow, the way a clock moves from 6 to 9. RIGHT: a small clock face, centre (1060, 360), circle 360 px across (thin dark outline, 5 px, pale cream #FFF8E7 fill) with only the numbers 12, 3, 6 and 9 shown inside (36 px, bold, dark), a hub dot, a teal hand pointing at 6 and an amber hand pointing at 9; a curved amber arrow with an arrowhead outside the clock from 6 to 9 going the way a clock moves, labelled the way a clock moves (32 px, bold, dark) below the clock at (1060, 600). BOTTOM CENTRE, one line of bold text at y 735 (64 px, teal #0072B2): clockwise. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: A turn that goes the way the hands of a clock move, like 6 to 9, is clockwise.
images.description: An arrow pointing down and then left after a quarter turn, beside a clock whose hand goes from 6 to 9 the way a clock moves, with the word clockwise below.
images.context: Concept image for Clockwise and Anti-clockwise. It follows the idea of the clock hands that define clockwise movement in your maths book and shows the concept's own example of an arrow that turns from down to left.
images.teaching_notes: Place a finger on 6 and move it to 9 along the clock. The slip to watch is thinking that clockwise and anti-clockwise end in the same place after any turn.

image_decisions.why: The arrow and the small clock side by side show that a turn from down to left goes the way a clock moves.
